background_notes.fact: On the normalized torus Jf(x)=-f(-x) has Fourier coefficients -hat f(-k), is an involutive isometry on each H^s and mean-zero dot H^s, and preserves reality and mean zero. It acts on distributions by pullback. For the source PDE, u=JU satisfies u_t+u_xxx=u u_x, with datum J U0=q; the transformation is reversible.

background_notes.justification: Substitution x↦-x in the periodic Fourier integral gives the coefficient formula; reindexing nonnegative norm sums gives isometry, extended by completion or duality. The chain rule gives u_t=-U_t, u_x=U_x, u_xxx=U_xxx. The same equalities hold distributionally by change of variable in test functions, with the locally integrable square transformed by reflection. Applying J twice is the identity, so solution correspondence and uniqueness are preserved.

background_notes.fact: The multiplier S_t with symbol exp(i t k^3) is a strongly continuous isometry group on every H^s and mean-zero dot H^s. For a spatially smooth solution path of the target equation, v=S_{-t}u satisfies v'=S_{-t} partial_x(u^2)/2=B_t(v,v)/2, and ||v(t)||_H^gamma=||u(t)||_H^gamma.

background_notes.justification: The symbol has modulus one and obeys the group law. Strong continuity follows first on finite Fourier sums and then by their norm density and isometry. On smooth paths, termwise differentiation in any fixed lower Sobolev norm is justified by rapid Fourier decay; (S_{-t})'=partial_x^3 S_{-t}. Hence v'=S_{-t}(u_t+u_xxx)=S_{-t}partial_x(u^2)/2. The multiplier preserves every stated norm, including differences.

background_notes.justification: Truncation removes a nonnegative norm tail tending to zero and respects conjugate symmetry. Apply the supplied continuous dependence to these data; norm isometry transfers convergence to target flows. For every finite frequency set F, coefficient convergence gives sum_F <k>^(2 gamma)|hat f(k)|^2<=A^2 from a common bound A. Taking the supremum over finite F gives the full bound. If the bound initially holds a.e., continuity of the H^gamma norm and density of a full-measure subset of [0,T] extend it to every time. This is a lower-semicontinuity argument, not an exchange of an uncontrolled infinite sum with a limit.

background_notes.fact: A smooth periodic datum belongs to every integer Sobolev space. A flow continuous in H^n for every positive integer n is spatially smooth at every time; the source solutions obtained at the different integer exponents agree by E001 uniqueness. The target smooth flow then has enough time regularity to differentiate its twist in any fixed Sobolev space.

grounds.reason: Existence and uniqueness for every positive exponent and source equation.

background_notes.justification: Integration by parts gives arbitrarily fast Fourier coefficient decay for smooth data. Conversely, for each j choose an integer n>j+1/2; Cauchy–Schwarz bounds sum_k |k|^j |hat f(k)| by ||f||_H^n times the finite square root of sum_k <k>^(2j-2n). Thus the differentiated Fourier series converges uniformly, and f is C^j. The same estimate transfers time continuity from H^n to C^j. The PDE consequently has a continuous right side in each fixed Sobolev space (choose higher n for the three derivatives and the product). Integrating the distributional time equation gives C^1 time regularity there. These are routine regularity consequences of the supplied all-integer bounds, not an additional PDE existence theorem.
